note: nestor/triage/ + scripts/decision_triage.py — put the 200+ draft seal queue into themed groups and surface which rows are already resolved, so a human seals coherent batches instead of oldest-first-blind. Built by three parallel agents against a fixed contract (cluster / supersede / report), then audited. Assembly, not invention: the survey found every part already shipped in the fleet (willow-mcp nest/selflearn clustering shape, Nestor semantic_matcher/calibrate + the N1 rewording bench, Jeles conflict_scan stance, nestor.decision.propose_edge as the sink). Re-landed stdlib-only clean-room because Nestor's venv has no numpy/sklearn/networkx and the box cannot reach embeddings.

decisions.question: Before building the grouping, was the box searched for what already exists?
decisions.commitment: Yes — and only after the operator stopped a first attempt that jumped straight to building. Two look-sees (the fleet on disk; the open internet) ran first, exactly the discipline the before_build hook (#105) now enforces. They converged: grouping is an assembly of shipped parts (~100 lines), not a new capability, and building the clustering primitive fresh would have repeated the rediscovery `the-house-already-knew.md` documents. The triage re-lands the shapes over Nestor's own matchers rather than importing willow-mcp (unavailable, and heavy).
decisions.why: This is the recursive point of the whole session: the anti-rediscovery rule applied to its own next build. Searching first turned a from-scratch clustering system into a thin assembly with a clear sink, and the record of that search is itself the search path for the next seat.

decisions.question: What did the audit change about what the agents built?
decisions.commitment: Two defects, both caught by running it rather than reading it. (1) The default bar was 0.45, inherited from the rewording rank@1 bench — a different task; on all-pairs triage it flooded with 674 skeleton false-contradicts because question-shaped decisions share a 'Should the X be Y?' skeleton that character difflib scores. A --calibrate sweep put the knee at 0.55 (269 groups / 62 edges; the supersedes there are genuine 0.92+ rewordings), so the default moved and the reasoning was written down. (2) The --propose path had never been run and crashed: add_pair dedups same-question decisions on source_norm, so an edge's endpoint went missing; fixed with id-prefixed ephemeral rows. The two agents also died before writing their test files, so the audit wrote test_triage_supersede.py and test_triage_report.py — including the seals-nothing proof.
decisions.why: A green module the builder never executed is not done. The bar was a measured correction (state the knee, don't inherit it from a different task), and the crash was exactly the class the repo warns about — coverage is a claim about the harness: the agents' own tests were missing, so nothing had run the emit path until the audit did.

decisions.question: Can the triage seal anything?
decisions.commitment: No. Every path proposes and only proposes. render() touches no store; emit_edges() calls DecisionMemory.propose_edge only, landing draft edges (edge_sig='', verifier=''); the CLI --propose ingests into a throwaway in-memory store and asserts 0 pairs and 0 edges sealed before it returns. Proven end-to-end on the real 316: 'proposed 62 edges; 0 sealed'. The groups and edges are a queue for a human at nestor ui, never a verdict.
decisions.why: You may propose, you may not confirm. A tool that reconciles the seal queue is exactly where an agent would be tempted to also resolve it; the covenant says the reconciliation is proposal and the seal stays the human's, and the test that ingests a real store and asserts nothing sealed is that covenant made executable.
